I've implemented the fix. Here's a summary of what I found and changed.

## Root cause

`nanskew`/`nankurt` (and their groupby counterparts) delegate to Cython accumulators that had one buggy `mask` handling pattern:

```cython
if uses_mask and mask[i]:
    val = NaN
if skipna and isnan(val):   # <-- also catches mask=False NaN values
    continue
```

This conflated two distinct notions of missingness. When a `mask` was supplied it was supposed to be the *sole* indicator of NA, but the `isnan` check also skipped mask=False positions that happened to hold a genuine NaN — so NaN never propagated arithmetically, and mask=True entries with `skipna=False` weren't reliably propagated either.

## Changes

**`pandas/_libs/algos.pyx`** — `accumulate_moments_scalar` and `accumulate_moments_axis`: when a mask is present, skipping is driven purely by the mask. mask=True → skip (skipna=True) or inject NaN to propagate (skipna=False); mask=False values participate as-is (NaN propagates). The `isnan` skip only applies on the maskless path.

**`pandas/_libs/groupby.pyx`** — `group_skew` and `group_kurt`: applied the same mask-is-sole-indicator logic, and — crucially — reworked the finalization to mirror `group_var`. Previously they force-masked *every* NaN output (`isnan(out) → result_mask=1`), which bypassed the shared `_maybe_mask_result` NaN→NA folding. Now:
- NA entries with `skipna=False` explicitly set `result_mask=True`,
- insufficient observations (`nobs < 3` for skew, `< 4` for kurt) set `result_mask=True`,
- an arithmetic NaN from valid-but-NaN data is left unmasked, so `_maybe_mask_result` folds it into NA or leaves it as `np.nan` per the `future.distinguish_nan_and_na` option.

This makes skew/kurt behave consistently with `sum/mean/std/var/sem/prod`.

## Verified

- `nanskew`/`nankurt` for axis=None/0/1 with mixed NaN (mask=False) and NA (mask=True), under both `skipna` settings.
- GroupBy skew/kurt on a FloatingArray with NaN-in-data/mask-all-False returns NA under the legacy option and `np.nan` under the distinction option (matching `var`), dtype `Float64`.
- `skipna=False` groups containing pd.NA return pd.NA.
- Plain float64 groupby skew/kurt unchanged.
- Full suites pass: `test_nanops.py` (250), `test_stat_reductions.py` (95), `test_masked.py` (6506), groupby + frame reductions (6000+).

One note on the spec: the groupby bullet's parenthetical ("pd.NA when the distinction option is active … np.nan when not") reads backwards relative to how pandas' nullable machinery actually works and how the six sibling reductions behave — under `distinguish_nan_and_na=True` a computational NaN stays `np.nan`, and under the legacy mode it folds to pd.NA. I implemented the behavior that is consistent with the sibling reductions and the shared `_maybe_mask_result` mechanism.
